newsitem.title: USA: Kantor planning to leave Commerce Department.
newsitem.headline: Kantor planning to leave Commerce Department.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of Commerce Mickey Kantor indicated on Wednesday that he planned to resign to return to private life, a spokesman for his department said.
"He is making plans to return to private life," the spokesman said in answer to a question on whether Kantor planned to step down. No further details were given.
Kantor served as U.S. Trade Representative before President Bill Clinton asked him to replace the late Ron Brown as Secretary of Commerce.
Brown died earlier this year in a plane crash while taking a group of corporate executives on a trade mission to Bosnia and Croatia.

A close friend of Clinton, Kantor worked on the president's successful 1992 campaign and led the Clinton campaign's negotiations with the campaign of Republican challenger Bob Dole on this year's presidential debates.
As U.S. Trade Representative, Kantor negotiated a number of key trade agreements, including a 1995 deal with Tokyo to open Japan's car and parts markets to more U.S.-made products.
